posts.excerpt: This article is rendered by the same JSON block interpreter used in the blog-compose core module. Browse /blog on this docsite to preview every block type.

blocks.title: You are viewing the real engine
blocks.text: These blocks are stored as JSON in docsite/content/blog/posts.json and rendered with DocComposeRenderer — the same Compose document shape client sites use with ComposeBlogRenderer.
Each article is an ordered list of typed blocks. Explanation blocks support highlight and underline phrases — for example tempjs add-module and compose interpreter.

blocks.title: Add module
blocks.description: Copies engine files, Prisma model, /blog routes, and admin compose editor.
blocks.command:
tempjs add-module blog-compose
pnpm prisma db push

blocks.text: Blog posts as data — compose visually in admin or author JSON by hand.

blocks.caption: Image block — use any public path or CDN URL.

blocks.text: Read the full module guide at /developers/blog-compose or open the maintainer architecture page at /maintainers/blog-compose.
Future blog engines (rich-text editors) will use a different engine id and interpreter. This compose variant is the first building block for template blogging.

posts.title: Blog posts in your sitemap
posts.excerpt: When blog-compose and seo modules are installed together, /blog and every published slug are registered for sitemap.xml automatically.
posts.author: tempjs

blocks.text: The SEO module adds a static /blog route when SITE.features.blogCompose is true. Dynamic post URLs come from lib/blog/register-sitemap.ts, which registers each published slug with buildAppSitemap().

items: Install seo and blog-compose (or install blog-compose after seo)
add-module patches app/sitemap.ts to import register-sitemap
Publish posts in admin — slugs appear on next sitemap build

blocks.title: Requires database
blocks.text: Dynamic slugs are read from BlogPost rows. This docsite demo uses static JSON instead of Prisma.
